clue.text: I demand high standards in reception FT is running

indicators.note: running here means these letters are set loose and reshuffled into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A fussy person insists on top standards at the Financial Times front desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' shuffles RECEPTION, FT (the paper's initials) and IS into the answer; 'in' is only a link. The definition speaks in the first person, as the answer would describe itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who insists on flawless results is a stickler for getting everything exactly right.

clue.text: Officers on cruise ships getting contented noises around captain's table, finally

indicators.note: around means the purring sounds wrap about the letters picked next

parts.note: a cat makes purrs when it is contented

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of each of the words captain's and table

explanation.surface: Ship's officers enjoy happy murmurs at the captain's dinner table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the last letters of 'captain's' and 'table', S and E, and 'around' sets PURRS around them: PUR-SE-RS.
explanation.definitionFit: On a liner, the officer who handles money and passengers' affairs holds that title.

clue.text: Having no initial notice, advertisers mobilise back-up

indicators.note: mobilise means set in motion, so the remaining letters are moved into a new order
having no initial means the opening letters of the following word are dropped

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper

explanation.surface: Advertisers, lacking an opening announcement, call up their support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having no initial' removes AD from the front of ADVERTISERS, leaving VERTISERS, which 'mobilise' shuffles.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-time soldier held in reserve is called up as extra support when needed.

clue.text: Sign up tenant, dropping initial resistance

indicators.note: dropping initial means a letter at the front of the word is let go

parts.note: a renter is someone who pays rent, a tenant
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A landlord signs up a new tenant after their initial reluctance fades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping initial' takes R off the front of RENTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol for something, such as a race or competition, is to put your name in for it.

clue.text: Time's right to open shop for small fish

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
an outlet is a retail shop

explanation.surface: Now is the moment to open a store selling little fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to open' puts R at the front of OUTLET, giving ROUTLET, after T.
explanation.definitionFit: A young trout, like a piglet among pigs, is a diminutive fish.

clue.text: Boost for broadcast, engaging international musician

indicators.note: engaging means taking on, so the scattered letters hold the next letter inside
broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A promotional push for a radio show brings in a musician from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns BOOST into OBOST, and 'engaging' puts I inside it: OBO-I-ST. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the oboe, a double-reed woodwind instrument, is a performer of music.

clue.text: Most of City trade nickel in recession — it's unyielding

indicators.note: in recession means going backwards, so the whole string is read in reverse
most of means all the word except its final letter is used

parts.note: a sale is a piece of trade
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

explanation.surface: Commerce in the City shrinks in a downturn, proving inflexible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' trims CITY to CIT; CIT + SALE + NI is then read backwards, as 'in recession' signals, giving INELASTIC. 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that will not stretch or give way is rigid and resistant to pressure.

clue.text: Sign part of mosaic including date

indicators.note: including means the tile word takes the next letter inside it

parts.note: a mosaic is built from small tiles

explanation.surface: A fragment of mosaic shows a symbol along with a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts D inside TILE: TIL-D-E.
explanation.definitionFit: The wavy mark over an n in Spanish is a diacritical symbol.

clue.text: Tree sheltering attempt to rear fragrant shrub

indicators.note: to rear means turned to the back, so the whole build is read backwards in this down clue
sheltering means the tree word keeps the attempt word inside it

parts.note: an elm is a tree
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A tree protects a young plant being raised beside an aromatic bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rear' reverses the whole build, ELTRYM, which suits a down clue read upwards; 'Tree' looks like the definition but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen with scented leaves and white flowers, sacred to Venus, is a sweet-smelling bush.

clue.text: Switch books to master italian dish

indicators.note: switch means turn about, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, books of the Bible
sir is a form of address to a master

explanation.surface: A cook trades in their cookbooks to learn a speciality from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: OT + TO + SIR makes OTTOSIR; 'Switch' reverses it all. 'to' supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice cooked slowly in stock until creamy is a classic course from northern Italy.

clue.text: Cover first slice of prime cut ham

indicators.note: cut means that letter is removed from the acting word

parts.note: to ham is to overplay a part on stage

indicators.note: first slice of means only the opening letter of prime is taken

explanation.surface: A deli worker covers the top slice of premium cut ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first slice of' picks P from 'prime', and 'cut' removes it from OVERPLAY. 'ham' is a verb, not meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer laid on top of something conceals or coats it.

clue.text: Return ferry stopping short, engineers making blunder

indicators.note: return means go back, so the whole string is read backwards
stopping short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a RoRo is a roll-on roll-off car ferry
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A ferry trip home cut short leaves the engineers committing a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping short' trims RORO to ROR; ROR + RE is RORRE, which 'Return' reverses. 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake or slip is a faux pas or gaffe.

clue.text: Will soldiers in reserves back trial at start?

indicators.note: at start means the trial word comes first in the answer

parts.note: a test is a trial

indicators.note: in means the soldiers word sits inside the reversed reserves
back means the reserves abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
men are soldiers, as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: Will soldiers in the reserves support a trial run first?
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the reserves into AT; TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve. The question mark covers the surface's own question.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal document setting out how someone's estate is to be distributed after death.

clue.text: What's shown by facility to create crosswords?

definitions.text: What's shown by facility to create crosswords?

parts.note: facility means aptitude or skill
to set a crossword is to compose it, hence the word setter

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter's talent for compiling crosswords is on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' is the crossword term for composing a puzzle; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The range of abilities a person has is their repertoire of competences.

clue.text: Engage in battle to revise school rank (not top grade)

indicators.note: revise means rework, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not means the letter for the top grade is left out

parts.note: A is the top grade in exams

explanation.surface: Pupils get into a fight over revising the school's league table without an A.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes the A from SCHOOL RANK, and 'revise' shuffles the remaining SCHOOLRNK. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stags clash antlers when they fight, so the phrase means to come into conflict.

clue.text: Battied to break in, overcoming resistance

indicators.note: overcoming means the break-in word goes over and around the letter for resistance

parts.note: stove is a past form of stave, to stave in being to break in
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone fought to force entry despite meeting opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcoming' wraps STOVE around R: ST-R-OVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To have struggled or fought hard is to have made a great effort.

clue.text: See the sites of Middle East following head for section of Russian church

indicators.note: following means the pieces before it come after the head word

parts.note: onion is slang for the head, as in use your onion
to do a city is to see the sights as a tourist

explanation.surface: A tourist visits Middle Eastern sights before heading for an Orthodox church.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'do' a city is tourist slang for seeing it; 'use your onion' means use your head. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulbous roof typical of Orthodox churches is a feature of their architecture.

clue.text: Trade in shillings and pennies?

definitions.meaning: to trade in something is to swap it for something else
shillings and old pennies are former small coins, cash that has gone out of use

explanation.surface: Dealing in old British coins.
explanation.walkthrough: Shillings and pre-decimal pennies are British coins withdrawn in 1971: read as EX- (former) plus CHANGE (coins), they are old loose cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Swapping one thing for another is a transaction; former coins are loose cash no longer current.

clue.text: Discover fault -time for force

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: a defect is a fault
F is the physics abbreviation for force

explanation.surface: Finding a flaw means a time penalty for the police force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time for force' means T replaces F in DEFECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To find or notice something hidden is to uncover it.

clue.text: Smeared expert with teaching qualification

parts.note: a dab, or dab hand, is an expert
BEd is a Bachelor of Education degree

explanation.surface: A skilled teacher with a degree has been rubbed with something.
explanation.walkthrough: DAB is British slang for an expert, from 'dab hand'. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Patted on lightly with something wet or greasy, leaving marks.

clue.text: Challenging former performance

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
acting is performance on stage

explanation.surface: A one-time star's stage work proves demanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Demanding great effort or precision makes a task tough.

clue.text: Waffles after consuming litre drinks

indicators.note: consuming means the waffle word takes the litre letter inside it

parts.note: to gas is to chatter or waffle

explanation.surface: Someone eats waffles after downing a litre of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' puts L inside GASSES: G-L-ASSES. 'Waffles' is a verb, not food; 'after' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumblers and wine goblets hold drinks, so the container stands for its contents.

clue.text: Made greeting including rank

indicators.note: including means the letters are held within the words made greeting

explanation.surface: Someone said hello, taking position into account.
explanation.definitionFit: A level or standing in a hierarchy is a grade or step.

clue.text: Woman's interrupting cook with quiet tip

indicators.note: interrupting means the woman word breaks into the cooking word

parts.note: to bake is to cook in an oven
she is a woman, and 's stands for is
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A woman breaks in on a chef with a quiet word of advice.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion gives BAKSHEE before the last piece. 'tip' means a gratuity, not a rubbish dump or a hint.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Middle East and South Asia, a small sum given as a gratuity or alms.

clue.text: Broke UK apt to go to pieces

indicators.note: to go to pieces means to fall apart, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Britain is likely to collapse financially.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken or no longer working, from the German for done for.

clue.text: Old costume seen round northern island group

indicators.note: seen round means the costume word is placed around the next letter

parts.note: a toga was the garment of ancient Romans

explanation.surface: Ancient dress is worn by people in the north of an archipelago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen round' puts TOGA around N: TO-N-GA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Polynesian kingdom made up of some 170 islands in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Get wind up, mostly about vote in state

indicators.note: about means the shortened word goes around the next letter
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to wind up is British slang for tease
X is the mark a voter puts on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: People get irritated by a ballot in some province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims TEASE to TEAS, and 'about' puts it around X: TE-X-AS. 'Get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lone Star State is one of the fifty in the US.

clue.text: Agent in ancient city backing ruler

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the whole build is reversed
in means the agent word sits inside the city word

parts.note: Rome is an ancient city
a rep is a sales representative, an agent

explanation.surface: An envoy in an old city supports a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses ROREPME, the agent placed in the city, to give the ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign of an empire, such as Napoleon or the Roman Caesars, rules it.

clue.text: Toxic debt forms after chairman's last steer

indicators.note: after means the debt forms are placed behind the other pieces
last takes the final letter of the word chairman

parts.note: a steer is a young castrated bull, an ox
IOUs are written promises to repay a debt

explanation.surface: Bad debt mounts once the chairman's final steer on policy arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steer' is not guidance but a bullock. 'chairman's last' is the final letter N, the possessive adding none.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmful or poisonous, as noxious fumes are.

clue.text: Vulgarity: flogging senseless tat on Sabbath

indicators.note: flogging means beating, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Selling silly junk on the holy day is in poor taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flogging' is British slang for selling, which suits the surface, but here it signals beating letters into shape. 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of refinement or good judgement is crudeness.
